youtube.title: 40 Minutes Before the Iceberg, the Titanic Told a Warning Ship to "Shut Up"
youtube.description:
On 14 April 1912, ships including the Noordam, Caronia, Baltic, Amerika and Mesaba sent the Titanic warnings about ice. Around 11 pm, the Californian, stopped nearby in field ice, called again; its signal was so loud it nearly deafened Titanic's wireless operator Jack Phillips, who was busy sending passengers' messages. "Shut up, shut up! I am busy!" he replied. The Californian's operator turned off his set and went to bed. At about 11:40 pm, lookout Frederick Fleet reported "Iceberg, right ahead." The Titanic sank at 2:20 am; more than 1,500 people died, and lifeboats left with hundreds of empty seats.

📂 Case File #036: The Titanic's Warnings

Sources: National Geographic, "Despite the warning 'Iceberg, Right Ahead!' the Titanic was doomed"; Museums Worcestershire, "Sunday April 14th 1912".
Images (Wikimedia Commons): RMS Titanic (1912); the iceberg believed to have sunk Titanic; SS Californian; Titanic's Marconi room; Jack Phillips (RMS Adriatic); presumed Titanic lifeboat (public domain).
